entities.summary: Lingnan architecture, or Cantonese architecture, refers to the characteristic architectural style(s) of the Lingnan region – the Southern Chinese provinces of Guangdong and Guangxi. Usually, it is referring to the architecture associated with the Cantonese people, with other peoples in the area having their own styles. This style began with the architecture of the ancient non-Han Nanyue people and absorbed certain architectural elements from the Tang Empire and Song Empire as the region sinicized in the later half of the first millennium AD. Lingnan architecture is a architectural style with roots in Asia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lingnan architecture played a significant role in shaping the cultural identity of Southern China, particularly during the Tang and Song dynasties. Its unique blend of architectural elements influenced the development of Cantonese architecture and left a lasting legacy in the region.
